entry.summary: An electronic travel authorisation (eTA) before flying to Canada. Not needed when arriving by land or sea.
entry.pre_arrival: Apply for the eTA through Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada only.
entry.other: A criminal record, including a drink-driving conviction, can bar entry. Children travelling without both parents should carry a consent letter.

tourism.route: eTA when travelling by air; valid passport for most land or sea arrivals
tourism.detail: Australian passport holders do not need a visitor visa. Visits are normally allowed for up to six months, but an eTA only permits travel to request entry.
tourism.next: Apply through the official CAD $7 site before booking a flight and verify that the approval contains the correct passport number.

meetings.detail: The visitor must stay under six months, avoid directly entering the Canadian labour market, and keep the main business, remuneration and profits predominantly outside Canada. Meetings, negotiations and qualifying training are published examples.
meetings.next: Carry the foreign-company support letter, Canadian invitation, relevant contracts, funds and a host contact available within 24 hours.

conference.detail: Meetings, conferences, conventions and trade fairs are published business-visitor activities. An eTA remains the separate air-entry requirement.
conference.next: Carry registration and agenda documents; if the role changes from attendee to presenter, classify it under the speaker exemption.

unpaid-speaking.detail: A guest speaker may work without a permit for the sole purpose of making a speech or delivering a paper at a dinner, graduation, convention or similar function. The regulation does not make the exemption depend on the absence of payment.
unpaid-speaking.next: Have the organiser state the exact function, speech or paper, date, audience and whether any other teaching, consulting or seminar work is included.

paid-speaking.route: IRPR 186(j) guest-speaker exemption or commercial speaker/seminar exemption lasting no more than five days
paid-speaking.detail: The regulation separates a guest speech or paper at a specified function from a commercial speaker or seminar leader delivering a seminar of no more than five days. It does not publish a no-pay condition, but work outside those words requires another exemption or permit.
paid-speaking.next: Have the host distinguish a single guest speech from the full duration of a commercial seminar, document all payments and classify any extra consulting or teaching separately.

book-launch.route: Business visitor for publisher and rights meetings; IRPR 186(j) for a qualifying author speech; local publisher or bookseller for retail
book-launch.detail: A launch should be divided into meetings, public talk, signing and sales. Business visitors representing a foreign business may sell to a Canadian business but may not make sales to the Canadian general public under the published business-visitor rule.
book-launch.next: Ask the publisher to classify the author talk, handle Canadian retail and record whether a signing or workshop adds work beyond the exempt speech.

ai-teaching.route: IRPR 186(j) for an exact speech or seminar, or the short-term high-skilled work public policy; otherwise a work permit
ai-teaching.detail: A qualifying commercial seminar may last no more than five days. Separately, TEER 0 or 1 work can be exempt for up to 15 consecutive days if the exemption was not used in the prior six months, or up to 30 consecutive days if not used in the prior 12 months. A publicly funded university researcher may have a separate 120-day lane. Formal or recurring teaching is not automatically covered.
ai-teaching.next: Have the university or event host confirm the NOC/TEER occupation, exact duties, total consecutive days and previous use of the short-work exemption.

remote-work.route: Digital nomad on visitor status for self-employment or an employer outside Canada
remote-work.detail: Canada expressly states that digital nomads may work online for themselves or an employer outside Canada while visiting for up to six months because they are not entering the Canadian labour market.
remote-work.next: Keep contracts, clients, employer, invoicing and principal business outside Canada; obtain a work permit before accepting Canadian employment or moving into the local labour market.

entrepreneur.route: LMIA-exempt significant-benefit entrepreneur work permit or a qualifying CPTPP investor route
entrepreneur.detail: Canada allows an entrepreneur to seek an LMIA-exempt work permit where the proposed Canadian business would create or maintain significant social, cultural or economic benefits or Canadian jobs. The federal Start-up Visa Program stopped accepting new applications on 30 June 2026. CPTPP can facilitate qualifying Australian investors with substantial committed capital, but it still requires the immigration criteria and a pre-arranged position or arrangement.
entrepreneur.next: Do not build a new plan around the paused Start-up Visa. Prepare a significant-benefit and jobs case or test the investment and role against CPTPP before operating.

trade.route: Business visitor for sourcing, orders, meetings and trade fairs; CPTPP for qualifying investor, professional, technician or intra-company work
trade.detail: Business visitors may buy Canadian goods or services and take orders while keeping remuneration and profits abroad, but may not sell to the Canadian general public. CPTPP removes the labour-market test for specified categories but requires wage, education, experience and pre-arranged-contract safeguards where applicable.
trade.next: Separate negotiation and order-taking from installation, fulfilment, direct retail and local employment; have the Canadian partner identify the business-visitor or CPTPP category.

artist.route: IRPR 186(g) short-term performing-artist exemption when every condition fits
artist.detail: The exemption can cover a solo or group artistic performance and integral staff where the person is part of a foreign production or group, or a guest in a Canadian production, has a time-limited engagement and is not in an employment relationship with the Canadian contracting organisation. Performances primarily for film, television or radio are excluded.
artist.next: Have the promoter document the production, guest status, limited dates, contractual relationship, payment and whether film, broadcast or continuing employment is involved.

mixed-mission.route: Use the eTA for entry and map every active act to business visitor, IRPR 186, short-work, CPTPP or work-permit authority
mixed-mission.detail: Canada offers several flexible exemptions, but an eTA alone does not confer a right to work. A conference-attendance lane does not automatically cover teaching, Canadian clients, retail sales or a performance on the same trip.
mixed-mission.next: Give one lead Canadian host a complete activity and payment schedule and carry written evidence for each exemption or permit at the border.

laws.rule: The recreational use of marijuana (Cannabis) is subject to local laws and regulations. It's illegal to transport marijuana (Cannabis) across Canada's international borders (including the United States), even if you are entering or leaving the country. If you break the law, you can receive criminal penalties, including jail time. Make sure you know the local cannabis laws about: legal age possession purchase sharing impairment production Local health authorities have reported illegal drugs may be mixed with more potent substances that can lead to health issues including overdose and death.

laws.rule: To drive in Canada, you may need: an International Driving Permit (IDP) and a valid Australian licence Get an IDP before you leave Australia. You can drive for up to one year with an IDP and your Australian licence. After that, you'll need a local driver's licence. Requirements may vary in different provinces and states. For details see Driving in Canada.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Canadian Dollar (CAD). You can change Australian dollars at commercial banks and exchange bureaus. Declare all amounts over CAD$10,000. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. Credit and debit cards are widely accepted.
